payload.objective: Find the molecular mechanism that best explains the loss of function of BTK-p.Arg28His. The targeted test should be the reference-versus-variant structure prediction of the PH domain (structure_comparison), to see whether the substitution changes the predicted local structure.
payload.question: For a pathogenic missense variant in an immune-deficiency gene, which molecular mechanism best explains the loss of function, and does a targeted computational test change the conclusion that the starting evidence suggested?

payload.statement: ClinVar classifies NM_000061.3(BTK):c.83G>A (p.Arg28His) as Pathogenic (criteria provided, multiple submitters, no conflicts; 2 of 4 stars; 8 submissions; last evaluated 2025-02-06) for not provided, X-linked agammaglobulinemia, X-linked agammaglobulinemia with growth hormone deficiency.
payload.strength: criteria provided, multiple submitters, no conflicts (rank 2 of 4, clinvar_review_status)

payload.statement: The abstract reports that a downregulating PH-TH domain mutation (R28H) linked to X-linked agammaglobulinemia impairs BTK activation at the membrane and in the cytosol by preventing PH-TH dimerization.

UniProtKB natural variant VAR_006220 at residue 28 (R to H): Autosomal recessive agammaglobulinemia 1; XLA; moderate; X-linked agammaglobulinemia with growth hormone deficiency; X-linked agammaglobulinemia. 6 publications cited.

The abstract reports molecular dynamics with MM-PBSA binding free energies for BTK PH-domain mutants and classifies R28C/H, together with K12R, K19E and E41K, as "functional mutations" rather than "folding mutations" (L11P, S14F, F25S, Y40N).
gnomAD v4.1: allele X-101375202-C-T observed 1 times in 1097783 alleles (frequency 9.11e-07; 0 hemizygotes, 0 homozygotes).

The abstract proposes that an IP6-dependent PH-TH dimer may activate BTK during B-cell receptor signaling, and reports that the constitutively active E41K mutation activates BTK by stabilizing this IP6-dependent PH-TH dimer.
Ensembl VEP predicts missense_variant for NM_000061.3:c.83G>A (NP_000052.1:p.Arg28His; exon 2/19; MANE Select ENST00000308731.8).

The same article's abstract (indexed in OpenAlex) states that the R28H PH-TH mutation linked to X-linked agammaglobulinemia impairs BTK activation at the membrane and in the cytosol by preventing PH-TH dimerization.

UniProtKB function of BTK_HUMAN: Non-receptor tyrosine kinase indispensable for B lymphocyte development, differentiation and signaling (PubMed:19290921). Binding of antigen to the B-cell antigen receptor (BCR) triggers signaling that ultimately leads to B-cell activation (PubMed:19290921). After BCR engagement and activation at the plasma membrane, phosphorylates PLCG2 at several sites, igniting the downstream signaling pathway through calcium mob…
UniProtKB annotates residues 28 of Q06187 as Binding site: 1D-myo-inositol 1,3,4,5-tetrakisphosphate; evidence: experimental evidence used in manual assertion; PubMed 10196129.
The retrieved abstracts do not report a measured binding or dimerization assay showing how R28H changes PH-domain affinity for IP6, Ins(1,3,4,5)P4 or PIP3; the MD study is computational only.
payload.why_it_matters: Without a measured binding change, it is unclear whether R28H acts mainly through lost ligand binding or through the dimerization defect, and these point to different rescue or correction strategies.

payload.statement: InterPro annotates residues 3-135 of Q06187 as domain: Pleckstrin homology domain; evidence: match to sequence model evidence used in automatic assertion.

The retrieved literature does not state whether R28H reduces BTK protein level or stability in B cells, or whether the loss of function is purely a signaling defect; the MD paper's "functional" label is an inference from binding free energy, not a cellular measurement.
payload.why_it_matters: A stability defect (folding) would predict a different mechanism from a dimerization or signaling defect, and the current evidence does not separate the two.

payload.statement: AlphaMissense gives p.Arg28His of Q06187 a AlphaMissense pathogenicity of 0.9978, classed as likely pathogenic (AlphaMissense class) (scale: 0 to 1; higher = more likely pathogenic).
payload.strength: computational prediction, not validated for clinical use

payload.statement: The retrieved abstracts do not identify which PH-domain contacts involving Arg28 are lost in the IP6-dependent dimer, so the structural basis of the R28H dimerization defect is not established.
payload.why_it_matters: Knowing the Arg28 contact partners would show whether the His substitution breaks a salt bridge or changes local geometry, which matters for judging whether the defect is specific to His or general to any change at position 28.

payload.strength: computational prediction, not validated for clinical use

payload.strength: computational prediction, not validated for clinical use

payload.summary: BTK R28H literature collected from Europe PMC and OpenAlex. The main finding (PMID 38971313) is that R28H impairs BTK activation by preventing IP6-dependent PH-TH dimerization; an MD study (PMID 24307874) classifies R28C/H as functional rather than folding mutations, but this is computational only. Gaps: no measured binding or dimerization assay for R28H, no cellular stability data, and no mapped Arg28 contacts.

PDB entry 1BWN (X-RAY DIFFRACTION, 2.1 Å, deposited 1998-09-25) observes residue 28 of Q06187: PH DOMAIN AND BTK MOTIF FROM BRUTON'S TYROSINE KINASE MUTANT E41K IN COMPLEX WITH INS(1,3… ; ligands 4IP, ZN.

PDB entry 6TT2 (X-RAY DIFFRACTION, 1.36 Å, deposited 2019-12-23) observes residue 28 of Q06187: The PH domain of Bruton's tyrosine kinase mutant R28C; ligands ZN, MG; the residue is mutated in this entry (R28C).
AlphaFold DB model AF-Q06187-F1 covers the full sequence of Q06187 (mean pLDDT 84.44).
ClinVar lists NM_000061.3(BTK):c.82C>T (p.Arg28Cys) at the same residue as Pathogenic (criteria provided, multiple submitters, no conflicts).
EVE gives no score for p.Arg28His of Q06187 (state not_covered).
payload.why_it_matters: Only AlphaMissense, ScoreCons and popEVE are available for this substitution, so the computational picture rests on three predictors.

payload.why_it_matters: No functional assay in the returned data measures this residue, so the effect of R28H on BTK activity or PH-domain function is not measured in this run.

payload.why_it_matters: No returned structure shows R28H itself, and whether residue 28 touches the bound inositol phosphate or other ligands is not known from this run.

Subject BTK-p.Arg28His (Q06187, R to H). Evidence E1-E19 and gaps G1-G6 are recorded. Form at least 2 agent-generated hypotheses of different mechanism classes (for example PH-TH dimerization defect vs. IP6/PIP3 binding defect vs. folding or stability change), each with supporting evidence IDs, a refutation criterion and a starting rank, then hand off.

payload.statement: Agent-generated hypothesis: R28H disrupts the IP6-dependent PH-TH dimer interface. Arg28 contributes contacts that hold the two PH-TH units together, and the His substitution weakens them, so BTK cannot be activated at the membrane or in the cytosol.
payload.would_refute: Arg28 side chain makes no atom contact (within about 4 Å) with the partner PH-TH protomer in any dimer model or experimental dimer structure, and the modelled R28H dimer keeps the same interface contacts and interface energy as wild type.
payload.label: agent-generated hypothesis
payload.rank_rationale: Ranked first because E2 and E8 state directly that this exact R28H substitution prevents PH-TH dimerization, which is the only exact-substitution mechanistic claim in the record. Still unsupported by any measured dimerization assay (G1) and the contacts lost are not identified (G3). Not a measured result.

payload.statement: Agent-generated hypothesis: Arg28 is a direct contact for the inositol phosphate head group in the PH-domain pocket. His loses the guanidinium-phosphate interaction, which lowers ligand affinity and prevents the membrane-recruitment step that activates BTK.
payload.would_refute: In ligand-bound structures 1B55 and 1BWN, no atom of residue 28 lies within about 4 Å of the bound 4IP ligand, and a modelled R28H complex shows a binding free energy change below about 0.5 kcal/mol relative to wild type.
payload.label: agent-generated hypothesis
payload.rank_rationale: Ranked second. UniProt annotates residue 28 as an inositol-tetrakisphosphate binding site (E10), and two ligand-bound structures exist (E15, E16). E4 reports MM-PBSA binding changes for R28H, which supports this class, but the MD is computational and the ligand contacts by residue are not returned (G6). No measured affinity data exist (G1).

payload.statement: Agent-generated hypothesis: R28H destabilises the local PH-domain fold, lowering folding stability or cellular abundance of BTK. Less BTK protein is available to reach the membrane, which reduces signalling.
payload.would_refute: A predicted structure of R28H shows the same local backbone and side-chain packing as wild type (per-residue RMSD below about 1 Å across residues 1-135), the predicted stability change is near zero, and the R28C experimental structure 6TT2 is essentially identical to wild type in the PH domain.
payload.label: agent-generated hypothesis
payload.rank_rationale: Ranked third. The only support is conservation and pathogenicity scores (E12, E13, E14) and a confident model (E18). E4 explicitly classes R28H as a functional rather than folding mutation, and E2 attributes the defect to dimerization. Kept as a competing class to test, not as a favoured mechanism. No stability or abundance data exist (G2).

payload.summary: Three agent-generated hypotheses are recorded for BTK-p.Arg28His. H1 (protein_interaction, rank 1) says the substitution weakens the IP6-dependent PH-TH dimer interface. H2 (ligand_binding, rank 2) says it removes an inositol-phosphate head-group contact. H3 (stability_folding, rank 3) says it destabilises the PH fold. Plan a structure-comparison test (R28 vs H28 in the PH domain, dimer models, and 1B55/1BWN contacts) that can refute each, with the refutation criteria in the hypotheses. Note the record has no measured binding, dimerization, or stability data (G1, G2, G5).

payload.description: Reference (R28) versus variant (H28) structure prediction of the BTK construct (residues 1-143) with the same provider (esm_atlas). Tests whether R28H produces a confident local rearrangement near the PH domain (H3) and whether contacts at the site change (weak support for H1). Does not directly test ligand binding (H2).
payload.expected_learning_reasoning: A confident local rearrangement or changed site contacts would raise H3 and give some support to H1, moving the ranking. A matching fold is uninformative under the catalogue's own controls, and single-substitution predictions are not validated, so a null result would move the ranking little. H2 is barely touched. Moderate-low learning.
payload.feasibility_reasoning: esm_atlas can_run true with inference; cached_examples also available; construct residues 1-143 cover residue 28; one existing result. Run time is bounded by the 120 compute-second cost, which fits the 300 s remaining. Some risk from the provider.
controls: Same provider, model version and construct for both sequences.
Residues with low confidence in either model are masked before the RMSD is computed.

payload.description: Lists experimental structures covering residue 28 that hold a non-solvent ligand and whether residue 28 neighbours that ligand (RCSB), with shortest distance, negative and selectivity controls. Directly tests whether Arg28 contacts the bound inositol phosphate (H2), and gives a weak contact signal for H1 if the contact is with a partner.
payload.expected_learning_reasoning: A contact between residue 28 and an inositol-phosphate ligand in 1B55 or 1BWN would support H2 and move it up. Absence of any contact in the 39 ligand-bound structures would weaken H2 toward H1 or H3. Outcomes move H2 in opposite directions, so the ranking can change. Limited because crystal contacts with soluble analogues do not measure binding by the variant, and no R28H structure exists (G6).
payload.feasibility_reasoning: can_run true; 39 structures observe residue 28 with a non-solvent ligand; zero compute seconds, two tool calls, no approval needed.
controls: Negative control: ligands in the same structures that never list the residue as a neighbour.
Selectivity control: number of distinct residues that neighbour the contacting ligand, so a contact is not an artefact of a large neighbour list.
Site-state control: structures in which the residue itself is mutated are reported separately.

payload.description: FoldX predicted folding free-energy change for R28H on the AlphaFold model (via EBI ProtVar), with local pLDDT at residue 28 and the values for other substitutions at the same residue. Tests the stability route (H3) against a near-zero change.
payload.expected_learning_reasoning: A destabilising ddG at or above threshold with adequate pLDDT would support H3 and move it up. A neutral value would weaken H3 but does not show the variant is tolerated, so the ranking of H1 and H2 would not change. Prediction error near 1 kcal/mol limits the outcome. H1 and H2 are not tested.
payload.feasibility_reasoning: FoldX prediction state ok; zero compute seconds; two tool calls; no approval needed. Value not known until run, and pLDDT at residue 28 must be high enough for interpretation.
controls: Within-site comparison: the same predictor for the other substitutions reported at this residue.
Applicability control: the model confidence (pLDDT) at the residue, because FoldX on a low-confidence region is not interpretable.

payload.description: Whether residue 28 lines a pocket predicted by P2Rank or ProtVar on the AlphaFold model, and whether it lies in a predicted protein-protein interface. Weak test of the ligand pocket (H2) and the interface (H1).
payload.expected_learning_reasoning: Pocket membership would weakly support H2 and an interface hit would weakly support H1. The interface state for this residue is not_covered, so the H1 signal is likely empty. Predicted pockets are not measured binding sites, so the outcome cannot move the ranking much.
payload.feasibility_reasoning: ProtVar pocket data answer for this residue; P2Rank runs on the AlphaFold model; zero compute seconds; two tool calls; no approval.
controls: Rank control: the rank and probability of the pocket among all predicted pockets of the model.
Confidence control: mean pLDDT of the pocket residues.

payload.rationale: Scores: T1 structure_comparison learning 0.35, feasibility 0.8, cost 120 compute s and 3 tool calls with approval. T2 ligand_contact learning 0.55, feasibility 0.95, cost 0 s and 2 calls. T3 stability_effect 0.4, 0.9, 0 s. T4 structural_context 0.25, 0.9, 0 s. By these scores T2 would be chosen, since it has the most learning per unit cost and tests H2, the current H1 rival, directly. The objective asks for the reference-versus-variant structure prediction, so I chose T1. It fits the remaining budget (120 of 300 compute s, 3 of 109 tool calls) and has an esm_atlas provider available. Note that T1 mainly discriminates H3 and only weakly H1, and it does not test H2. Its null outcome is weak because single-substitution predictions are not validated. T2 is the recommended next test if the objective is relaxed.

rejected.reason: Highest score by learning per cost (0.55, zero compute) and the only test that directly probes H2. Not chosen because the objective requests T1; recommended as the next test after T1 or if the objective is relaxed.
Learning 0.4 for H3 only; a neutral ddG would not separate H1 from H2. Zero compute, so it is a cheap follow-up to T1 if H3 needs a second check.
Learning 0.25; the interface state is not_covered so the H1 signal is likely empty, and predicted pockets are not measured binding sites.

payload.summary: Planner chose T1 (structure_comparison, reference vs R28H, esm_atlas, 120 compute s, requires human approval) as the objective requests, although T2 (ligand_contact) scored higher on learning per cost.
